subject: general
question: What is the main function of a master cylinder in a braking system?

options.text: To measure the brake fluid level
To build up hydraulic pressure to operate the brakes
To absorb vibrations from the road

solution:
The correct answer is __To build up hydraulic pressure to operate the brakes__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The master cylinder__ is a critical component of a vehicle's braking system.
 
• Its primary function is to convert mechanical force from the brake pedal into hydraulic pressure.
 
• This hydraulic pressure is then transmitted via brake lines to the brake calipers or wheel cylinders.
 
• It ensures that sufficient force is applied to the brake pads or shoes to stop the vehicle.
 
• The master cylinder contains a reservoir for brake fluid, which is essential for maintaining hydraulic pressure.
 
• Proper maintenance of the master cylinder is crucial for safe and reliable braking performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brake Fluid:**

 
 
• Brake fluid is a hydraulic fluid used in the master cylinder and brake lines.
 
• It transmits the hydraulic pressure needed to operate the braking system.
 
 
 
• **Brake Pads and Shoes:**
 
 
• Brake pads are used in disc braking systems, while brake shoes are used in drum braking systems.
 
• These components create friction to slow down or stop the vehicle.
 
 
 
• **Brake Calipers:**
 
 
• Brake calipers house the brake pads and are responsible for applying pressure to them.
 
• They are an integral part of disc braking systems.
